title: Cooperative lease backoff and staleness-aware queue tuner for continuous-batcher
author: Alyssa Chen
description:
Context: We observed intermittent starvation and long tail latency in continuous-batcher under mixed workloads (short stateless requests interleaved with KV-heavy long-context requests). Root causes: aggressive slot acquisition semantics that allowed long KV-warmup requests to hold batch slots while short requests accumulated, and absence of a staleness-aware aging signal for queued items. This PR introduces a cooperative lease-backoff mechanism plus a staleness-aware queue tuner and lightweight kernel hints to reduce tail latency and prevent starvation without sacrificing throughput.

Design summary: 1) Cooperative lease backoff: requests acquire a soft lease for a batch slot. Long-running requests that exhibit prolonged KV-warmup or kernel contention will yield their soft lease after an adaptive backoff period (exponential with capped jitter). Yielding returns the request to the queue as a higher-priority "warmup-assisted" token so the runtime can try a different compatible slot or schedule smaller micro-batches to keep throughput high.
2) Staleness-aware queue tuner: we compute a per-request staleness score that increases over time but gets a boost if the request is KV-cold (no KV cache hits) or was preempted. The queue's admission policy uses a combined score (age + staleness + fairness credit) to select the next candidate for batching, thus preventing indefinite starvation of older or cache-miss requests.
3) Kernel-hint metadata: admission path propagates a lightweight hint derived from request shape (sequence length, past token delta) so the kernel selector can prefer smaller kernels for mixed-size batches, reducing kernel mis-schedules that cause head-of-line blocking.
4) Timeouts & safety: per-request soft-timeout with jittered probe windows to avoid synchronized yield storms. Feature flagging and a kill-switch are provided: redwood.scheduler.cooperative_backoff and redwood.scheduler.staleness_tuner.

Implementation notes: changes touch scheduler admission logic, batcher coordinator, KV cache metrics plumbing, and the kernel hinting interface. New modules: scheduler/lease_backoff.go (adaptive backoff logic), scheduler/staleness_tuner.go (scoring and fairness credits), admission/kernel_hints.go (hint propagation), plus unit/integration tests and e2e perf harness updates. Backwards compatibility: default flags are off; when enabled the system maintains existing semantics for requests without hints.

Benchmarks: micro-benchmarks run on a 4-GPU dedicated node with mixed synthetic workload (40% short stateless 64-token requests, 60% KV-heavy 2k-token requests with high cache miss ratio). Key results vs main (feature off): - 95th percentile p99 latency for short requests down by ~8% (from 230ms to 211ms). - Tail latency (p99.9) for mixed workload down by ~15%. - Aggregate throughput sustained ~+6% under the same budget due to fewer wasted warmup slots. - KV-cache warmup rate improved: cold-to-warm transition latency reduced by ~12%. These results include canary A/B runs; see attached bench summaries.

Testing & validation: extensive unit tests for backoff math and scoring, integration in the continuous-batcher harness, and an extended perf canary (3-day run) against representative production traces. Safety checks added to prevent thrashing: minimum lease hold time, capped backoff multiply, and back-pressure if the admission queue grows beyond a configured threshold.

Rollout plan: feature-gate behind redwood.scheduler.cooperative_backoff and redwood.scheduler.staleness_tuner. Rollout steps: enable at 1% traffic -> monitor fairness/latency/cold-miss regressions -> 10% -> 50% -> full. Metrics to watch: batch slot utilization, per-request wait-time distribution, KV-cache hit rate, canary error budget, and kernel mis-schedule counts. Emergency rollback is a single flag flip.

Notes and follow-ups: - There is scope for tying the staleness score to long-running model-level signals (e.g., KV eviction pressure) as a future follow-up (ENG-1896). - Suggested follow-up PR: move kernel-hint scoring into the compilation stage so the kernel selector learns profile-based preferences across deployments.

Checklist: implementation, unit tests, integration tests, bench harness updates, docs snippet for flags, canary plan, and metrics dashboards added.

review_comments: Priya Nair: Nice design. Two asks: (1) can we make the backoff multiplier configurable per-class; (2) please add assertion that yielded requests don't lose trace/span linkage.
Alyssa Chen: Addressed both; added per-class multiplier and span-preserve shim in admission. Updated tests.
Jared Thompson: Observability looks good but please add a histogram for "yield_count" per-request so we can detect thrashing; also add an alert to canary dashboard if yield_rate > 0.5%.
Alyssa Chen: Added yield_count histogram and dashboard tile. Canary playbook updated.
release_notes: Introduces cooperative lease backoff and a staleness-aware queue tuner for the continuous-batcher to reduce tail latency and prevent starvation in mixed KV workloads. Feature gated; off by default.
